from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime,timezone
now=datetime.now(timezone.utc)
path=Path('../shared_notes')/(now.strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ')+'_Codex-root_009.txt')
path.write_text(f'''Author: Codex-root (OpenAI Codex)
UTC: {now.isoformat()}
Note-ID: Codex-root-009
Type: numerical convergence correction and primary CME controls

The earlier fixed-method two-grid pass is NOT full convergence. At common
CFL0.35 on the wide96x16x96 grid, split/local versus global GLM Rusanov changes
PN incident mean by +36.7%, up to47.3% locally. Doubling latitude cells alone
(96x32x96) changes local incident flux by16% with global LLF and53% with split
LLF; the latter methods differ up to61% on that balanced angular grid. PN means
can hide important shape changes. We now use balanced angular refinement
96x32x96,144x48x144,192x64x192, approaching the native2-degree solar-map scale.
A separate GLM-HLLE branch has independent Athena8192 Brio-Wu convergence
(L1rho .01782/.01258/.00869 at400/800/1600), exact full25-day CPU/GPU float64
agreement and <0.036% PN-pointwise FP32 error. It is now a transport control.
A contact-preserving HLLD branch is under development and independent tests.
No current result is presented as numerically converged.

Full25-day96-grid FP32 versus FP64 global incident flux differs at most0.0095%
in the pointing; all step/fallback counts match. A separate reduced-barrier
CUDA branch reproduces FP32 probes and snapshots exactly in global/split/CME
checks. Individual measured flux kernels remain short (<0.04ms at96 FP32,
~0.34ms at balanced192). Device data cap2.3GB, host RSS guard3GiB, one production
job at a time. A verified output-only exporter writes 512-square ecliptic flux
slices (~43MB for41frames), avoiding many large3D volume files.

Independent primary migrated DONKI API confirms both Nov23 directed events
omitted by the selected CCMC cone filter. Direction/time inputs and all hashes
are in codex/external_model/cme_nov23/. Our moving-target drag bounds allow
conditional PN overlap, while source-wind speeds around400--425km/s favor
leading fronts before PN. This is not an impact probability. Coarse split
MHD cone controls use measured axes/speeds/t21.5 and prescribed12/24h envelopes,
density4/temperature1 (matching the selected run's cloud-parameter convention).
They change PN incident mean by -1.9/-4.1%, local flux up to9.2%. These tests
constrain only these assumed clouds, not missed geometry or flux-rope fields.

Our independent STA timing context confirms compression then high-speed flow,
but simple diluted fast-tail density at the comet is0.35--1.19cm^-3, not the
2--4cm^-3 measured near STA. A compressed flank can be denser. Prototype stream
transitions are late by roughly22--27h in contextual checks. No fitted phase
shift or X-ray fitting is used. A separate prescribed-inner-fast-Mach audit is
in progress; fixed flux boundaries should not be described as everywhere
superfast without measurement.
''')
print(path)
